title: Growth & Go-to-Market

title: Funds & Fundraising
description: Make the next chapter possible. We help fund builders and founders articulate their vision, build relationships, and approach the right conversations with confidence.

title: Brand & Storytelling
description: Make your value easy to see—and hard to forget. We turn complex ideas into clear positioning, meaningful stories, and experiences that bring people closer.

title: Leadership & Coaching
description: You do not have to figure it all out alone. Get a strategic partner, an honest sounding board, and support for the leader—and business—you want to become.

title: Innovation & AI
description: Move from emerging possibility to meaningful progress. We connect new technologies, market insight, and the people who can turn an idea into action.

title: Services
description: Explore Manifest’s approach to growth, funds, storytelling, leadership, and innovation.

title: Selected work
description: Explore Jen Tacheff’s work across growth, venture, brand, leadership, innovation, and social impact.

title: Google Global Accelerator
description: A global accelerator has a powerful story inside every company it supports. Jen’s work with Google Global Accelerator focused on bringing those stories forward: the founders, the technologies they were building, and the impact they could achieve. The engagement connected that storytelling to the visibility and effectiveness of global campaigns.

title: GoFundMe / Classy
description: New technology needs a clear place in the market. Jen supported go-to-market work for new AI and data products at GoFundMe and Classy, connecting product direction, innovation, and brand visibility. The engagement brought a growth perspective to how emerging capabilities were introduced and how their place in the product roadmap developed.

title: Preston-Werner Ventures / ZEAL / RedwoodJS
description: Developer ecosystems grow through useful technology and the relationships around it. Working with Preston-Werner Ventures and ZEAL in a fractional CMO and COO capacity, Jen supported the visibility of RedwoodJS, developer and founder engagement, sponsorships, and partnerships. The work also included the inaugural RedwoodJS Conference for Builders in Grants Pass, Oregon.

title: The Go Game / Weve
description: The pandemic created a defining moment for The Go Game and Weve. Manifest led go-to-market strategy for the pivot, bringing together brand, marketing, product positioning, and growth. The work spanned a brand relaunch, a new product website, and a demo pipeline, giving the business a coordinated way to introduce its next chapter.

title: Noēsis / HumanConnections.AI
description: The future of AI brings technologists, researchers, investors, and policymakers into the same conversation. As a strategic partner and senior advisor to Noēsis, Jen helped create HumanConnections.AI and led workshops and initiatives with Harvard and Cambridge. Her work connected those conversations to organizational development, research collaborations, partnerships, and policy engagement.

title: W Fund / SWITCH
description: Building a company also means growing into a different kind of leader. At W Fund and SWITCH, Jen built and co-led a coaching program for executives and founders. The work brought her experience in company growth, branding, partnerships, and leadership into an environment focused on the people making the decisions.

title: Onramp
description: Growth work is strongest when commercial direction and product strategy stay connected. As Onramp’s CMO, CGO, and startup advisor, Jen led growth and go-to-market while advising on product. Her work helped the company secure customers including Twitch, Amazon, Google, Coinbase, and Vanguard, bringing a broad operating perspective to enterprise opportunity.

title: CommonGenius
description: At CommonGenius, Jen served as Vice President of Growth and Innovation, leading go-to-market and major activations at SXSW, TechCrunch, and Collision. Her work also included managing a creative studio that brought together experts, creators, influencers, and investors, connecting the platform’s market presence with the people and ideas around it.

title: Hustle
description: As Head of Brand, Marketing and Communications at Hustle, Jen worked across campaigns, partnerships, positioning, and go-to-market. Her remit included full-funnel initiatives with companies and institutions, alongside a digital portal for customer use cases, white papers, and stories. The role connected brand direction with the material needed to explain and support the product.

title: Women Who Code
description: As a founding leadership-team member and Vice President of Partnerships and Growth, Jen helped build the operations, revenue, partnerships, and programs behind Women Who Code’s global community. Her work connected company strategy with the infrastructure for local networks, international events, and partnerships supporting women in technical careers around the world.

title: Girls Inc.
description: A new center for girls in downtown Oakland required fundraising, public support, and a shared vision. As Girls Inc.’s Chief Marketing and Advancement Officer, Jen led marketing and fundraising for a capital campaign exceeding $20 million. Her remit connected board and executive leadership with campaign communications, events, corporate programs, and launch strategy.

title: Chabot Space & Science Center
description: At Chabot Space and Science Center, Jen’s work brought together public programming, membership, partnerships, and special projects. As Manager of Corporate Relations and Special Projects, she created and led programs connecting people with science, including emerging-professional initiatives, speaker series, exhibitions, and relationships with prominent figures and organizations in science and culture.

title: MotherCoders
description: Organizational transitions bring questions about funding, leadership, and the story of what comes next. Jen supported MotherCoders across fundraising, marketing, and leadership succession, including the founder’s transition out of the CEO role. The work combined strategy, pitch-deck development, and practical support, alongside introductions to people and opportunities in the wider ecosystem.

title: Jubilee Productions / THE DIVISIBLE
description: Jubilee Productions’ first short film needed more than a strong creative vision. Jen joined THE DIVISIBLE as an associate producer, contributing marketing guidance, fundraising support, and ideas for reaching potential contributors. Co-founder Marcus T. Thomas describes her as a key partner in the company’s establishment and the film’s inaugural launch.

title: Alana Karen
description: For a leader with a story to tell, visibility can begin with finding the confidence to tell it. Jen supported technology leader, author, and speaker Alana Karen with marketing and positioning. Alana describes that partnership as a turning point in her ability to present her experience and build a public voice.

title: Founder & creative advisory
description: Founder support takes different forms at different stages. Across separate engagements, Jen has helped founders clarify their stories, explore growth opportunities, develop confidence, and move projects forward. Recommendations from Kula Project, Yayble, Huggnote, VR Perspectives, The Broadway Gram, and The Girlfriend Manifesto show how that work adapts to the person and the business.

title: UC Berkeley Haas
description: Jen’s work has also included teaching the disciplines behind company building. As a visiting lecturer at UC Berkeley’s Haas School of Business, she delivered workshops on growth, innovation, go-to-market, startups, entrepreneurship, and impact. The role brought her operating and advisory experience into an educational setting over a four-year period.

title: Sparks
description: Explore speaking, founder mentorship, AI and human connection, creative work, and the ideas behind Manifest.

title: Ideas get stronger when people come together
description: From founder workshops to conversations about AI and society, Jen’s work has often involved bringing the right people into a room. Her experience spans teaching, conference development, startup mentoring, and policy dialogue, connecting practical business questions with the communities that can help move them forward.

title: A sounding board for the people building next
description: Founders need room to think alongside the pressure to act. Jen’s mentoring work spans accelerator communities, startup programs, and individual founder relationships. It draws on experience in growth, brand, partnerships, and leadership, with support that can extend from an early coaching conversation into a longer relationship.

title: What should AI mean for human connection?
description: HumanConnections.AI brings a human question into the development of technology: how can AI support social connection and flourishing? Jen helped create the initiative and contributed as an advisor, connecting researchers, technologists, investors, and policymakers through gatherings, collaborations, and a broader conversation about the choices ahead.

title: Recognized for showing up for founders
description: Techstars named Jennifer Tacheff among its 2023 All-Star Mentors for the Techstars Anywhere Remote Accelerator. Announced in February 2024, the recognition celebrates mentors who went beyond expectations in supporting founders and building meaningful relationships within the accelerator community.

title: Stories that travel beyond the boardroom
description: A clear story can help a founder, an author, or a creative team find its audience. Jen’s work extends into books, independent film, and creative businesses, combining marketing and positioning with encouragement, fundraising support, and the relationships that help a project become real.

title: Five starting points for your next move
description: Launching a fund, scaling a company, and entering a new market ask different questions. Manifest’s work brings growth, capital, brand, leadership, and innovation into the same conversation. A useful starting point is the decision in front of you and what needs to change for that decision to succeed.
